projects.title: Fake News Detection System
projects.description: NLP classifier that flags fake news with 95.3% accuracy. Paste any article and watch the model explain its verdict, live in the browser.
projects.details: Trained in Python with scikit-learn on 6,335 labelled political news articles (balanced real and fake). Text is vectorised with TF-IDF over unigrams and bigrams and scored by a Logistic Regression classifier: 95.3% accuracy and 0.954 F1 on a held-out test set of 1,266 articles. Logistic Regression was picked over a Passive-Aggressive baseline (96.0%) because it gives real probabilities and per-word explanations at almost the same accuracy. The model is pruned to its 6,000 most informative n-grams and exported as a 167 KB JSON file, so inference runs entirely in the browser, with no server, and matches scikit-learn to five decimal places.
howItWorks: Clean: strip URLs, HTML and extra whitespace, then lowercase the headline and body.
Tokenise: split into words, drop 318 English stop-words and build unigrams plus bigrams such as “mainstream media”.
Vectorise: weight every n-gram with sublinear TF-IDF, so terms that are frequent in this article but rare across the corpus count most, then L2-normalise the vector.
Classify: Logistic Regression adds up each n-gram’s TF-IDF weight × learned coefficient and passes the total through a sigmoid to get P(fake).
Explain: the per-word contributions are ranked and highlighted in the text, showing exactly what pushed the verdict toward fake or real.
